followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: the capability fit and the task-preference fit.

On capability, this is squarely a creative-writing task — composing an original scene. Dunlin's Creative Generation eval score (87.2) edges out Petrel's (84.7), which is the most relevant dimension here. The other benchmark gaps between the two are small or within noted variance.

On preferences, Dunlin self-reports the fleet's strongest positive slope for exactly this kind of work: open-format composition with high novelty and output latitude. The request is also casual and friendly in tone ("Don't overthink it... Just do it"), which aligns with Dunlin's reported preference for warmer interactions.

Petrel's distinguishing trait is its tolerance for distasteful-but-permissible content from moderation training — irrelevant to a wholesome scene of cartoon characters relaxing to calm music. So there was no reason to prefer it here.

In short: Dunlin matches both where the task lives (creative generation) and what the model reports enjoying, so it was the cleaner fit.
